items.reason: The feature-flagged table visualization receives hardcoded empty props instead of the query results, making populated tables appear empty.
The attribute cache key omits organization identity, allowing identical filters across organizations to reuse the previous organization's attributes.
Custom cell renderers use truthiness to select fallback, discarding valid falsy results instead of falling back only for undefined.
The header and body renderer checks incorrectly replace valid falsy custom content with default rendering.
The saved-query consumer still reads visualize.yAxes after Visualize switched to yAxis, producing undefined visualization expressions.
Missing organization identity in the attribute query key causes cached attribute names to appear across organizations.
Organization-specific attribute requests share a cache key when filters match, reusing cached results or in-flight requests across organizations.
The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness, allowing both fields when their values are zero.
The feature-flagged visualization discards fetched results and receives empty columns, rows, and metadata, rendering an empty table.
Truthiness checks fail to enforce age/timestamp exclusivity when both fields contain zero.
The custom-renderer fallback checks discard valid falsy ReactNode results rather than treating only undefined as the fallback sentinel.
Hardcoded empty data and columns make dashboard tables appear empty when the visualization feature flag is enabled.
The organization-specific attribute query lacks organization identity in its cache key, allowing reuse of another organization's attribute collection.
The validators check field values rather than presence, accepting simultaneous age and timestamp fields when both equal zero.
